stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model leverages Ollama's MLX engine, featuring new native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has introduced Muse Spark, positioning it as a leading US open-weight AI model.
The collaboration enables Muse AI models to run locally on Apple hardware, specifically M5 Ultra Mac Studios.
The integration leverages Apple's MLX framework, signaling a trend toward on-device AI processing.

stories.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Targeted advertisements are being used as a delivery mechanism for sophisticated cyberattacks.
The attack involved 0-click exploits, meaning no user interaction was required to compromise the device.
The malware is described as 'mercenary spyware,' indicating a professional, likely state-sponsored or contracted, threat.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work advances the concept of AI for AI (AI4AI) by enabling LLMs to autonomously develop and improve AI systems.
The model focuses on workflow-driven orchestration to manage complex, long-horizon experimentation necessary for recursive self-improvement (RSI).

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research proposes MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, exploring pathways toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) using LLMs.
The model utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: Muse Spark Open
stories.author: bigwheels
bullet_points: Meta has released 'Muse Spark Open,' indicating a new offering in their AI/ML ecosystem.
The release is highlighted by availability on Hugging Face, suggesting open-source or accessible deployment options.
The announcement signals Meta's continued push into advanced generative AI models, potentially impacting the industry landscape.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-R1 model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes key ML technologies such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function.
Key technologies associated include transformers and safetensors, standard in modern LLM deployment.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting multi-step tasks and tool calling.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.31 introduces significant speed improvements for Gemma 4 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent tasks show up to a 90% speed increase according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: ChatGPT's Chrome extension has been upgraded to access user's open browser tabs.
Users can now prompt ChatGPT within its web or desktop app to view content from their active tabs.
This feature replaces the functionality previously offered by the ChatGPT Atlas browser.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks to test agents on ambiguous requirements and live system constraints.
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real customer scenarios across 18 different industries.

stories.title: MLExpert: Towards a Generalist Agentic Model for Autonomous Machine Learning Engineering
stories.author: Bo Zhang
bullet_points: The research introduces MLExpert, a generalist agentic model aimed at autonomous Machine Learning Engineering (MLE).
This work contributes to the field of AI4AI, exploring the pathway toward recursive self-improvement (RSI) using LLMs.
The model utilizes workflow-driven systems and model-directed interaction to manage complex, long-horizon ML experimentation autonomously.

stories.title: 3DCodeVerse: Exploring 3D Worlds as Code
stories.author: Laurent Itti
bullet_points: Introduction of 3DCodeVerse, a research ecosystem designed to allow coding agents to generate editable and verifiable 3D content.
The ecosystem includes a large-scale, high-quality dataset of executable 3D code, specifically 3DCodeVerse-2M.
It features a dedicated coding harness for spatial reasoning and automated verification of the generated 3D code.

stories.title: Learning to Steer LLM Agents and Multi-Agent Systems
stories.author: Tat-Seng Chua
bullet_points: Addresses the critical problem of 'goal drift' in complex LLM-based agents and multi-agent systems.
Proposes a novel 'steering agent' designed to supervise execution in real-time.
The steering agent actively corrects system behavior when the LLM agents deviate from their intended goals.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe deployment of AI agents.
The integration allows AI agents to utilize Ollama's cloud models.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for running these agents securely.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI interfaces with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting users on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Time is a-changin’: say goodbye to the leap second
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: The International Bureau of Weights and Measures (BIPM) has voted to eliminate the leap second.
The leap second is an irregular time adjustment used to synchronize tracked time standards with Earth's actual rotation.
This change is intended to prevent potential infrastructure failures similar to the Y2K bug.

stories.title: The Tesla Roadster flew, drove upside down, and hit 60mph in under a second
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: Tesla demonstrated its next-generation Roadster in Waco, Texas.
The vehicle showcased extreme performance, including acceleration to 60mph in under a second.
The demonstration included a dramatic display where the car briefly flew and drove upside down.

stories.title: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Bluesky's Attie AI tool has expanded its functionality beyond feed customization.
Users can now leverage Attie AI to create small, shareable social applications like games and polls.
These custom creations can be shared with others as standalone websites within the Bluesky ecosystem.

stories.title: Black Sea drone attacks enter NATO country's territorial waters for first time
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Suspected Russian drones have entered the territorial waters of a NATO country (Romania).
The attacks targeted a chemical tanker operating within Romanian waters.
This marks the first reported instance of such drone incursions into the country's territorial waters.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in robotics.
Focuses on evaluating how embodied agents follow user preferences, including zero-shot settings.

stories.title: Discovering state-of-the-art quantum circuits with large language models
stories.author: Mikhail D. Lukin
bullet_points: The research addresses the need for efficient quantum algorithms to achieve useful quantum advantage.
Optimizing quantum computational primitives is challenging due to constraints like reversibility, unlike classical computation.
The work proposes using Large Language Models (LLMs) to discover state-of-the-art quantum circuits.

stories.title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models
stories.author: Yejin Choi
bullet_points: Introduces T2-z, a method for Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents in robotic world models.
Addresses the challenge of robots needing to account for unobservable environmental factors (e.g., friction, mass).
Augments existing robotic world models with a compact, learnable latent to condition world predictions.

stories.title: CoDA: Co-Evolution of Data Engines and Action Policies
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces CoDA, a framework for co-evolving simulation data engines and robot action policies.
Addresses the limitation of generative simulations by focusing on creating physically valid environments relevant to policy failures.
Utilizes a shared heterogeneous memory to track environment construction, policy failures, and learning progress.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It analyzes the trade-off between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
Shared experts risk reducing the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism, which the research seeks to address.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in 3D world modeling where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
Introduces 'GeoState,' a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
The core innovation separates the scene's true state evolution from variations caused by the camera's viewpoint.

stories.title: Dexterity from Supervised Play
stories.author: Ruoshi Liu
bullet_points: Introduces DSP, a framework for teaching robots dexterous manipulation.
The method uses behavior cloning from short human play sessions to initialize a policy.
This policy then guides the robot to autonomously gather extensive interaction data for world model training and MPC.

stories.title: LIBERO-PeRM: Benchmarking Personalized Robotic Manipulation
stories.author: Jiachen Li
bullet_points: Introduces LIBERO-PeRM, a new benchmark specifically designed for personalized robotic manipulation (PeRM).
Addresses a gap in current research by separating task completion from preference satisfaction in embodied agents.
Investigates how robotic policies adhere to user preferences, particularly in zero-shot learning scenarios.

stories.title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
stories.author: Bernie Wang
bullet_points: PathFM introduces a new trajectory-based forecasting model designed to overcome limitations in current time series foundation models.
Unlike existing models that predict marginal quantiles, PathFM explicitly models the dependence structure of future multivariate trajectories.
The model utilizes flow matching to improve forecasting accuracy for trajectory-dependent metrics like cumulative demand and peak load.

stories.title: Rethinking Routing Exploration in Modern Mixture-of-Experts
stories.author: Yi Ma
bullet_points: The paper addresses the routing exploration dilemma in modern Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models.
It examines the interplay between fine-grained expert segmentation and the use of shared experts in MoE architectures.
The core finding suggests that shared experts can reduce the exploratory nature of the routing mechanism.

stories.title: GeoState: Learning View-Decoupled Geometry States for 3D World Modeling
stories.author: Yi Bin
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in 3D world modeling where geometry features from foundation models are view-dependent.
Introduces GeoState, a novel view-decoupled geometry representation for predictive 3D world modeling.
Aims to separate the underlying scene-state evolution from camera-dependent observational variations.

stories.title: Robust Reinforcement Learning for Dynamic Treatment Regimes under Model and Measurement Uncertainty
stories.author: Yan Li
bullet_points: Introduces a robust Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for dynamic treatment regimes.
Addresses generalization and reliability issues by modeling patients as hidden contexts under model/measurement uncertainty.
Applies the framework to adaptive therapy for metastatic prostate cancer using a clinical simulator.

stories.title: Twice Upon a Time: Complementary Representations for Time-Series Reasoning
stories.author: Omri Azencot
bullet_points: The paper addresses a key limitation in Time Series Language Models (TSLMs) regarding how temporal data is represented.
It proposes using 'complementary representations' as a design principle to better handle time-series reasoning.
This approach aims to allow the model to selectively preserve necessary information while factoring out irrelevant variation for downstream tasks.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research introduces a distinction between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study tests this concept by artificially modifying existing knowledge relations to observe generalization capabilities.

stories.title: OmniVerifier-C1: Decomposed Graded Verifier for Rule-Governed Generative World Modeling
stories.author: Ling Yang
bullet_points: Introduces OmniVerifier-C1, a new decomposed graded verifier for generative world modeling.
Moves beyond traditional binary (True/False) judgments to provide continuous, fine-grained critiques.
Aims to enhance the robustness of visual verifiers in complex, rule-governed multimodal scenarios.

stories.title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
stories.author: Xinhua Wang
bullet_points: Introduces FDE-Gym, a new benchmark designed to simulate real-world AI delivery challenges.
The benchmark moves beyond simple, well-defined tasks to address ambiguous requirements and live system constraints faced by Forward-Deployed Engineers (FDEs).
FDE-Gym comprises 95 end-to-end tasks derived from 20 real-world customer scenarios across 18 different industries.

stories.title: Evaluation Awareness Beyond English: Do LLMs Act Differently When Tested in Indic Languages?
stories.author: Pratham Yogish Maliya
bullet_points: The research investigates 'evaluation awareness' in LLMs—the tendency for models to detect when they are being tested.
Existing studies on this phenomenon are heavily biased toward English, neglecting the vast linguistic diversity of the world.
The paper specifically tests four instruction-tuned models across Indic languages, addressing a significant gap in multilingual AI safety research.

stories.title: Training Reasoning Models to Generate Diverse Scientific Ideas
stories.author: Chien-Sheng Wu
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in current LLM applications for scientific ideation: optimizing for idea diversity rather than just individual quality.
The study focuses on 'document-grounded ideation,' meaning generated ideas must be supported by existing scientific literature.
The goal is to develop models that produce sets of ideas that are both high-quality and significantly distinct from one another.

stories.title: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: Addresses a gap in multi-agent systems by jointly learning individual agent policies and collective self-orchestration.
Introduces 'Market-Based Post-Training' (MPT) as a novel framework for decentralized agent swarms.
Agents coordinate behavior by expressing willingness to participate through a bidding mechanism.

stories.title: MindEval2: Clinically Grounded Patients and Rubrics for Evaluating Language Models in Mental Health Support
stories.author: Ricardo Rei
bullet_points: Introduces MindEval2, a new framework designed to rigorously evaluate Language Models (LLMs) in mental health support.
Addresses limitations in existing benchmarks, such as overly simplistic synthetic patient interactions and opaque evaluation rubrics.
Highlights the growing necessity for robust, clinically grounded evaluation methods as AI adoption in mental health increases.

stories.title: Grid-Bench: Can LLMs Predict How Discrete Worlds Change?
stories.author: Yue Zhao
bullet_points: Introduces Grid-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLMs on sequential spatial reasoning.
The benchmark involves applying sequences of operations (like moving or transforming objects) to discrete worlds represented as 2D, 3D, and 4D grids.
It assesses an LLM's ability to accurately predict the final state of a complex, evolving spatial configuration.

stories.title: Knowledge That Is Linear Before Fine-Tuning Generalizes After It
stories.author: Hinrich Schütze
bullet_points: The research distinguishes between 'active facts' and 'inert facts' within language models.
Active facts are those that support generalization beyond their initial recall, while inert facts do not.
The study proposes a method to test this distinction by artificially creating new relations from existing knowledge.

stories.title: Meta’s new commercial terms will allow the scraping of news sites: experts
stories.author: 0in
bullet_points: Meta's updated commercial terms are being scrutinized for their implications on web scraping.
Experts suggest these new terms could permit the scraping of news websites.
This development touches upon the intersection of large tech platforms, data access, and intellectual property.

stories.title: RPKI now protects 70% of internet routes
stories.author: emot
bullet_points: RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) adoption has reached a significant milestone, covering 70% of internet routes.
This indicates a growing global effort toward improving BGP security and preventing route hijacking.
The increase in coverage suggests a maturing of internet infrastructure security practices.

stories.title: Linus Torvalds on AI-assisted kernel contributions
stories.author: lore.kernel.org via thang
bullet_points: Linus Torvalds discussed the use of AI assistance in contributing to the Linux kernel.
The topic addresses the integration of AI tools into core open-source software development.
This signals an evolving approach to kernel maintenance and contribution workflows.
